name: colmap
why: Turns a pile of photos into 3D point clouds and surfaces via structure-from-motion, a real research pipeline you can run at home.

brief.what_it_is: COLMAP is a general-purpose Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS) pipeline with both a graphical interface and a command-line interface. It takes an image collection, either ordered or unordered, and recovers camera poses and a sparse 3D point model, then builds dense point clouds and meshes from those. It is free and open source under the new BSD license.
brief.why_it_exists: The project describes itself as a general-purpose SfM and MVS pipeline for reconstruction of ordered and unordered image collections. Its citation list ties the work to academic papers from CVPR, ECCV and ACCV, so it is presented as a research-grade tool rather than a consumer app.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives no step-by-step mechanism. The homepage says SfM is a robust incremental pipeline that recovers camera poses and sparse structure, and MVS uses PatchMatch stereo plus stereo fusion to produce dense point clouds and meshes. A GLOMAP global SfM pipeline and a vocabulary-tree image retrieval engine are also included.

commands_seen.context: Installs COLMAP from the conda-forge channel, one of the listed install routes in the README.

brief.install_notes: Pre-built binaries for Windows are on the GitHub releases page; Linux, Unix and BSD packages are listed via repology.org; Docker images are at hub.docker.com/r/colmap/colmap; conda packages come from conda-forge. Python bindings (pycolmap) install from PyPI, with a separate pycolmap-cuda12 package for CUDA-enabled wheels. Building from source is documented at colmap.github.io/install.html. The homepage's install selector is script-driven, so its per-platform commands did not show up in the fetched text. Sample datasets are available from demuc.de, or you can use your own images, then run the automatic reconstruction.
brief.standout: It is a complete, research-backed SfM and MVS pipeline that also ships a GUI, so you can run the full photo-to-mesh workflow with a single click or from the command line. Its Python bindings expose most of the pipeline, and the same tool is widely used in academic and industrial 3D reconstruction work.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the evidence shows. The GitHub README lists active core maintainers and a 2016-2026 copyright line, and the GLOMAP global SfM pipeline was published at ECCV 2024. I could not see a release date or last commit date in the fetched pages, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: AMD GPUs are only supported via HIP/ROCm when building from source. Building with third-party dependencies (ceres-solver, poselib, sift-gpu, vlfeat) may affect the license of the resulting build, since those are licensed separately. The homepage text is mostly feature blurbs and the install instructions sit behind a selector, so the exact install steps for each platform need the install guide. Dense reconstruction needs a sizeable amount of compute, though the README does not state specific hardware requirements.
quotes: COLMAP is a general-purpose Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS) pipeline with a graphical and command-line interface.
Use the automatic reconstruction to easily build models with a single click or command.
Dense reconstruction with PatchMatch stereo and stereo fusion to produce detailed dense point clouds and meshes.
